Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: encounter/_slot_name_not_set. MytesNormal.cs:14 declares Slots => ['first','second']. MYTES_NORMAL (myte.py:85) is `MytesEncounter(id='mytes_normal')` -- no slots= argument, so it inherits Encounter's default () (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py). MytesEncounter.create_monsters (myte.py:81-82) also never assigns `.slot_name` on either created Myte (it hands 'first'/'second' only to the constructor's private `slot` kwarg, myte.py:33-40, used solely to pick the opening-move branch). C#'s own mechanism reads the SAME fact from a different place: Myte.cs:53-54 gates its ConditionalBranchState on the LIVE `base.Creature.SlotName == 'first'/'second'`, which is only meaningful because CombatManager.AddCreature (CombatManager.cs:848-851) sorts/derives SlotName from the encounter's declared Slots row at creature-add time. The sim's re-architecture (constructor-time flag instead of a live attribute) reproduces the OBSERVABLE branch outcome correctly (verified by `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e4.py mytes-slot`: myte1 opens TOXIC_MOVE, myte2 opens SUCK_MOVE, matching Myte.cs:53-54's intent exactly) but leaves the actual `.slot_name` attribute None on both Mytes and the encounter's own `.slots` empty, instead of ('first','second') and 'first'/'second' respectively. DORMANT today: the only three sts2_rl/ consumers of `.slot_name` are `combat.sort_enemies_by_slot_name` (no-ops because MYTES_NORMAL.slots is empty) and sts2_rl/monsters/base.py's `get_next_slot`/`last_free_slot` (the other two) -- Mytes never summons, so neither of those two is ever consulted for this unit. Same family as encounter/the_obscura's Slots entry (LIVE there) -- see that record for the site where the identical omission has an observable consequence.

RoomType.rationale: MytesNormal.cs:16 RoomType => Monster. 'mytes' sits in hive's normal_keys only. Cross-ref seam/rooms_and_map (unaudited) for the runtime resolution mechanism; this record verifies only the per-encounter value.

HasScene.rationale: MytesNormal.cs:18 => true (custom combat-room .tscn layout); NCombatRoom.cs is the sole non-Models reader, purely scene/rendering. The sim has no scene layer.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: Presentation/bestiary only (ActModel.cs:169, NBestiary.cs:194). C# value is [Myte] (1 element), matching GenerateMonsters' single monster class. No sim counterpart, no observable cost.

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: MytesEncounter.create_monsters -> [Myte(hooks, rng, slot='first'), Myte(hooks, rng, slot='second')] (myte.py:81-82)
GenerateMonsters.rationale: MytesNormal.cs:32-39 returns a fixed 2-element array in source order: (Myte,'first') then (Myte,'second') -- roster {Myte}x2, ORDER first-then-second, ZERO Rng draws (a literal array initializer, no random call). The sim's override builds [Myte(slot='first'), Myte(slot='second')] in the identical order with zero draws -- roster, order and draw-count all match. The slot LABEL half of each returned tuple is reproduced in observable effect (see the Slots hook for the structural gap in how it is carried, which does not change this hook's own roster/order/draw-count verdict).

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.cs:39 => false. MytesEncounter is a plain dataclass subclass, never registered with the HookSystem; only the two Myte Monster instances register themselves. Matches C#.

guards.rationale: Not overridden; inherits Monster => (10, 20), matching sts2_rl/rewards.py GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER] exactly (`py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e4.py gold-ladder`). Poverty out of scope per PROMPT.md.
Neither overridden. MYTES_NORMAL passes no should_give_rewards= (default True); 'mytes' is absent from every weak_keys tuple, matching IsWeak=>false.
GenerateMonsters draws ZERO values on either side -- no draw here to misattribute to a shared stream. Stream seeding itself belongs to seam/rng_streams.
